course_name_original: Introducción a los Sistemas de Potencia de Energías Renovables, Tracción Eléctrica y Eficiencia Energética
course_name_en: Introduction to Renewable Energy Power Systems, Electric Traction and Energy Efficiency

learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.

Write, interpret scientifically and communicate orally documents in the field of the master's master's degree's main lines (electric power systems, electric and hybrid vehicles, energy efficiency and renewable energies), to specialised audiences.
Know the main multidisciplinary scientific journals focused on the master's degree's main lines, as well as the main public and private R+D+i institutions relevant to these lines.
Teamwork skills, recognising the different roles within a group and the different forms of organisation of work teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis.
Ability to assimilate and communicate technical and economic information written in English.
Ability to plan and organise their work.
Ability for critical reasoning, decision making and judgements formulation, based on information that includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity.
Skills of initiative, entrepreneurship, concern for quality and motivation for achievement.
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems for generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies and the constructive elements and materials of the Electrical Power Systems
Understanding the fundamental characteristics, as well as advantages and drawbacks of electrical and hybrid traction systems compared to combustion engines
Knowledge and ability to explain and argue the importance of power systems in the management of electrical energy.
Understanding and ability to explain and argue the technological foundation upon which sit the power system.
Identification of the different applications of power systems in the three trend topics of the master: power systems, electric / hybrid vehicle and energy efficiency.
Understand the energy pricing process, understanding the different components of the final price and pricing of electricity.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Sustainable Transportation: Electrical and Hybrid Electric vehicles
Competences and career development in the Electrical Power Systems and Sustainable Transportation field
Introduction to elaboration and communication of scientific/technical reports
assessment_rules: The final grade for the ordinary examination period is calculated as: Final grade = 0.9 × TR + 0.1 × AT. For AT to contribute positively, students must have attended at least 80% of the sessions. As a prerequisite for passing, students must satisfactorily complete specific tasks related to basic software environments. For part-time students, the final grade is calculated as TR, and attendance is not considered. The extraordinary examination period consists of the submission of an individual technical report (TRE), and the final grade corresponds to the grade awarded for this report.
